events.title: AI-driven formal proof search advances mathematics research
events.one_liner: AI-driven formal proof search has matured into a practical research tool for mathematics. Carnegie Mellon's Jeremy Avigad and colleagues developed Stellar Colosseum, a model-agnostic harness that allocates inference across proof strategies. On TCS-Bench (research-level theorems from FOCS, STOC, SODA), Colosseum achieved 71.0% accuracy using Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.7 Flash; Codeforces evaluation solved 218 of 222 problems.

sources.label: Carnegie Mellon University Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences

takeaways: Stellar Colosseum achieved 71.0% accuracy on TCS-Bench research-level theorems
Solves 218 of 222 Codeforces problems with Gemini 3.1 Pro and execution feedback
Direct-model performance: Gemini 3.1 Pro 30.3%, DeepThink 52.0%, GPT-5.6 Pro 68.0% on TCS-Bench
CMU Jeremy Avigad leads work in Lean proof assistant and Mathlib formalization
Connected to NSF-funded Institute for Computation and AI for Research in Mathematics (ICARM)

events.title: Phones impede learning: Evidence from a massive phone-free classroom experiment
events.one_liner: A three-year study across 43,000 middle and high schools published by the National Bureau of Economic Research found that Yondr magnetic phone pouches achieved 30–80% reduction in cellphone usage but did not improve test scores, attendance, or classroom attention. In year one, disciplinary incidents rose and well-being fell; by year three, these effects reversed, suggesting benefits may emerge as schools adapt.

sources.label: Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences

takeaways: 43,000+ schools studied over three years using Yondr phone pouches
Achieved 30–80% reduction in cellphone usage during school day
No improvement in test scores, attendance, or perceived cyberbullying
Year 1: disciplinary incidents rose, well-being fell; year 3: reversed to prior levels
Researchers: phone-free environments not 'simple or quick fix'; long-term benefits may emerge

The action repeals Biden-era regulations requiring 90% carbon capture by the 2030s, rescinding the 2009 endangerment finding and all remaining greenhouse gas standards for power plants.
takeaways: Eliminates emissions limits on coal and gas-fired power plants, September 14, 2026
Repeals 90% carbon capture requirement for existing coal and new gas plants by 2030s
Projected additional 123 million metric tons CO2 over next decade
Saves power plant operators $370 million in compliance costs
Repealed regulations included mercury and toxic metal restrictions; announced at G20 Houston

takeaways: Insufficient sleep (<7 hours/night) stronger predictor of longevity than diet or exercise
Only smoking had stronger association with life expectancy in first model
County-level US survey data, 2019–2025, controlled for physical inactivity, employment, education
Sleep physiologist Andrew McHill: correlation strength was unexpected
Observational study; cannot prove causation; recommends 7–9 hours nightly

The breakthrough expands options for highly sensitized patients previously considered untransplantable.

sources.label: Medical University of Vienna / Medical News

takeaways: 37-year-old dialysis patient with zero compatible-donor probability (cPRA value)
12+ years on waiting list with two previous failed transplants
Teclistamab treatment over 31 weeks achieved sustained antibody reduction
Case published in New England Journal of Medicine, July 2026
Led by Georg Böhmig and Martina Schatzl at MedUni Vienna

takeaways: 2.76 million living individuals and 294,000 deceased individuals affected
October 2025 to July 2026; discovered July 16, 2026

Failures in encryption at rest, access management, and monitoring
DMDC liable for FedRAMP, FISMA, NIST 800-171 compliance; DoD requires CMMC Level 2 for contractors
